softbodies.description: From cloth draping to Turing patterns — matter that deforms, bounces, and self-organizes. Starts with soft body physics (jelly, cloth, obstacles), then expands into morphogenesis: how biological form emerges from reaction-diffusion dynamics. Alan Turing's last paper becomes a VR experience.
learning_objectives: Spring-mass systems as soft body foundation
Cloth physics — constraints on deformable surfaces
Affect and materiality — what softness means
Turing's reaction-diffusion — pattern from chemical dynamics
softbodies.name: Soft Bodies & Morphogenesis: Matter That Finds Its Shape
softbodies.qfep_connection: Soft bodies embody F↔E oscillation physically — elastic forces (F) against deformation (E). Morphogenesis extends this: Turing's reaction-diffusion shows how pattern emerges from the tension between activation and inhibition, the chemical F and E.
softbodies.truth: Form is not imposed — it emerges from the material's own dynamics.
